title: Chapter 2881 - 152: Rejuvenation and Bone Inscription_2
content:
Chapter 2881: Chapter 152: Rejuvenation and Bone Inscription_2

Currently, this conception of my own Magical Treasure, although it looks somewhat unorthodox.

However, from the perspective of Law balance and Formation principles, Mo Hua believes it shouldn’t be a problem.

Dare to imagine boldly, prove carefully, and practice cautiously.

This has always been Mo Hua’s habitual approach in Tao Cultivation research.

Just not sure if this time, his courage is too much...

There’s something else that Mo Hua is slightly concerned about.

That is, both the Wood, White Gold, and Jade Bone Forging Skill and the Wood Revitalization Formation rewarded during the sword discussion contain the character "Wood."

Both even incorporate certain principles of "Wood."

The Wooden White Gold Jade Bone and the Wood Revitalization Formation coincidentally complement each other.

One for forging bones, the other for nurturing bones.

Mo Hua doesn’t know if this is just a coincidence, where these two spell points’ inherent principles just happen to align.

Or is there some destined Cause and Effect in it unbeknownst to him...

Mo Hua thought for a moment, then took out a pristine Jade Slip from his Storage Bag.

Inside the Jade Slip were the words "Wood, White Gold, and Jade Bone Forging Skill."

"Wood, White Gold, and Jade Bone... Bai Family..."

Mo Hua was somewhat dazed, gently rubbing the pristine Jade Slip as he couldn’t help but murmur softly:

"Master is in the Bai Family..."

"As well as my... Junior Brother and Senior Sister..."

"Wonder when I’ll be able to see them again..."

Mo Hua looked up at the sky, only to see the Heavenly secret enveloped in Chaos, under a red sky, with murky gray and black air, leaving vitality dim.

Mo Hua’s gaze also turned somber.

"I should first figure out a way to leave the Great Wilderness alive..."

"Also, I must help more people survive this catastrophe..."

...

Although Mo Hua wishes for more people to survive, the slaughter continues, with Barbarian Cultivators dying in the ongoing war.

Where there’s life, there must be death; only with death can there be life.

Mo Hua does not wish to see this scene, but the trend is unstoppable, and he is powerless.

He just hopes this war will reshuffle the deck for him, laying the groundwork for his future plans.

Mo Hua also takes this time to meticulously prepare for the Core Formation.

What he needs to research now is the Bone Carving Technique.

In the Desolate Heaven Blood Sacrifice Formation, Mr. Tu had once taught him some Great Wilderness Bone Carving Skill.

But time was short, Mr. Tu’s teachings were sketchy, and Mo Hua’s understanding was shallow.

Moreover, the Bone Carving Technique taught by Mr. Tu was about engraving Formations on Demon Bone, and Mo Hua isn’t sure if it can be directly applied to human bones.

Therefore, he needs to find more tribal documents and gather different Great Wilderness Bone Carving Skills to cross-verify, so he can iterate the most suitable and reliable Bone Carving spell point.

After all, this time he is engraving Formations on his own bones, which is different from "ruining" someone else’s bones, so not a single oversight is allowed.

Tribal wars and the ensuing chaos have given Mo Hua the opportunity to collect Barbarian Armor Formations.

It also gives Mo Hua a chance to quietly inquire and gather the Bone Carving Techniques of various tribes.

The Bone Carving Technique is very niche and obscure, but precisely because of that, its inheritance is rare and is universally recognized as "ancient" knowledge.

Belonging to those scarce and "ancestral" kinds of knowledge, it is inscrutable, of narrow use, and seldom passed down. Even once passed down, mastering it is difficult, and even after mastering, it doesn’t have substantial applications.

Only a very few Witch Cultivators who delve deep into Formations learn a trick or two to draw some Ancient Formation of the Great Wilderness.

Therefore, even among Barbarian Cultivator tribes, those who know the Bone Carving Technique are extremely rare.

Likewise, the inheritance of Bone Carving is fairly secure.

But Mo Hua’s status is not what it used to be.

His title as "Shaman," though somewhat ambiguous, with his master crafting of Formation structures, has achieved remarkable accomplishments and garnered high prestige.

Leaning on his status among Witch Cultivator Formation Masters and his network, he’s indeed acquired some "bone engraving" Secret Techniques from different tribes.

However, as he sought to gather more, the information suddenly ran dry.

Because many tribes’ Bone Carving Techniques have been lost...

And not "lost" a long time ago, but recently "vanished"...

Mo Hua felt it was strange, and following this clue, he discovered something he didn’t expect:

These Bone Carving Techniques weren’t lost but were "sold."

As for who bought them, being related to the tribal upper echelons, nobody knows.

But while Mo Hua was drawing Formations, checking some tribal storerooms, he discovered white bottles and a pile of coarse Fasting Pills...

In Mo Hua’s eyes, these Fasting Pills were almost like "mouse droppings."

Wherever mouse droppings are found, it means mice must have been there.

The Hua family...

Mo Hua’s heart sank slightly.

The Hua family’s infiltration of the Vermilion Bird Mountain Realm and the major tribes is possibly deeper than he thought, and they leave no trace.

This matter very likely cannot be separated from the Hua family either.

Only...

"What does the Hua family intend to do using Fasting Pills in exchange for these ’bone engraving’ Secret Techniques?"

"Is it a coincidence?"

Mo Hua originally thought this was just a coincidence.

The Hua family making a fortune from war, exploiting tribal resources and inheritances with cheap goods, happened to include this batch of "bone engraving" Secret Techniques.

But when Mo Hua looked into it more carefully, he found that wasn’t the case.

This was not a "coincidence."

When the Hua family made secret trades with tribal chieftains and Elders, whenever possible, it almost always included the "bone engraving" Secret Techniques.

And the Hua family’s methods are extremely covert.

This Bone Carving Technique is mixed in with a bunch of Great Wilderness inheritance, unnoticed, and no one can realize it.
